reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable space. Fix globally twice continuously Frechet differentiable f:E->R,real kappa,h and natural J. Assume kappa>=1,J>=2,h>0,and for all base points z and vectors v in E,
  (1/(2kappa))||v||^2<=D^2 f(z)[v,v]<=||v||^2.
The gradient is the genuine first-derivative Riesz representative. On Fin(J)={0,...,J-1},define exactly
  t_i=(h/2)(1-cos((i/(J-1))pi)),
  ell_j=the actual real Lagrange cardinal polynomial at these nodes,
  Lambda=sup{sum_j |ell_j(s)|:s in [0,h]},
  omega_ij=integral_0^{t_i}(t_i-s)ell_j(s)ds,
  b_j=integral_0^h ell_j(s)ds,
  c_j=integral_0^h(h-s)ell_j(s)ds.
The quotient uses real coercions,the supremum is real,and integrals are ordinary Lebesgue Bochner interval integrals. If h Lambda<=1/(65536kappa),put a=exp(-h/2),sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)). For z=(X,P) and noise zeta=(u,v),define
  P0(z,zeta)=a P+sigma u,
  Y0_j(z,zeta)=X+t_j P0(z,zeta),
  Y1_i(z,zeta)=Y0_i(z,zeta)-sum_j omega_ij grad f(Y0_j(z,zeta)),
  Phi(z,zeta)=(X+h P0(z,zeta)-sum_j c_j grad f(Y1_j(z,zeta)),
               a(P0(z,zeta)-sum_j b_j grad f(Y1_j(z,zeta)))+sigma v).
All sums use the J actual indices. Let G be the centered identity-covariance standard Gaussian probability measure on E and Gamma=G x G,an independent product of the two Gaussian vectors used for the two refreshes. Define the exact phase quadratic form and raw cost
  Q_kappa(x,p)=(1/(2kappa)+1/2)||x||^2+<x,p>+||p||^2,
  C_kappa(s,sprime)=ENNReal.ofReal(Q_kappa(s-sprime)),
  P_kappa(alpha,beta)=inf{integral^- C_kappa dpi : pi measure on S x S,
                         pi.fst=alpha,pi.snd=beta},
where S=E x E and phase subtraction is coordinatewise. Thus P_kappa is phaseWassersteinSq,an unrooted extended-nonnegative quadratic transport infimum.
Then there exists a single Markov kernel K from S to S,whose output at every incoming state is a probability measure,such that for every z in S,
  K(z)=(zeta -> Phi(z,zeta))_*Gamma.
For this same K,for every pair of probability measures mu,nu on S,the following three conclusions hold simultaneously:
  K composed with mu=(mu x Gamma)_*Phi,
  K composed with nu=(nu x Gamma)_*Phi,
  P_kappa(K composed with mu,K composed with nu)
    <=ENNReal.ofReal((1-h/(65536kappa))^2) P_kappa(mu,nu).
Kernel-measure composition is the updated measure obtained by integrating the transition law K(z) against the input measure;the displayed identities equate it to the actual independently-noised numerical-map pushforwards. Both updated laws use exactly the same fixed K and Gamma. The raw transport infimum ranges over all measures with the specified marginals and uses lower integration. No optimal-coupling,finite-moment or finite-cost convention is imposed. The coefficient is the square of the explicitly displayed real factor before applying ENNReal.ofReal;no square root of P_kappa is taken in this theorem.
The Hessian hypothesis is the normalized global C2 interface with lower coefficient 1/(2kappa) and upper coefficient 1. No target measure,invariant law or stationarity hypothesis/conclusion is supplied. The theorem concerns one-step contraction of arbitrary probability input laws through the actual direct-gradient two-stage kernel;it does not state a mixing-to-target result,an iteration-history assertion,query complexity,an approximate proximal interpreter or extra Gaussian arrays.
